findings.finding: Time-driven e-prop has already been translated into an event-driven recurrent-spiking implementation with continuous dynamics, weight updates, strict locality, sparse connectivity and reported scaling to millions of neurons without loss of learning performance.
findings.impact: Direct ordinary prior art for semantically active event-triggered eligibility localization; positive SparkBrain resource results do not imply mechanism novelty.

findings.finding: SparseProp gives numerically exact event-based sparse SNN simulation/training while avoiding full-neuron iteration per spike, with stated per-spike complexity reduction from O(N) to O(log N) and >4-orders-of-magnitude speedup in a million-neuron sparse LIF simulation.
findings.impact: A dense/current-implementation comparator alone is too weak for a broad efficiency claim; optimized exact sparse/event-driven data structures are an ordinary baseline.

findings.finding: ETLP implements three-factor local plasticity using pre-synaptic trace, post-synaptic voltage and a third factor that also acts as an update trigger, with reported computational-complexity advantage and FPGA proof of concept.
findings.impact: Delayed/global teaching signals do not require dense all-synapse visitation; trigger-driven local credit maintenance is established ordinary prior art.

findings.finding: Because stable SparkBrain globally decays every connection once per processed event while the strongest external baselines exploit sparse event structure, the meaningful discriminator is scaling/crossover under exact semantic equivalence across edge count, activity/event rate, active-degree, nonzero-eligibility-set size/lifetime and reward frequency.
findings.impact: A one-point sparse workload win is regime-specific SYSTEM evidence, not a general mechanism or architecture novelty claim.

novelty_or_reduction_impact: STRONG_ORDINARY_EVENT_DRIVEN_SPARSE_LOCALIZATION_REDUCTION_NO_MECHANISM_NOVELTY_UPLIFT.
